message.reasoning_content:
I need to adjust the card heights, move footer labels up. Keep three-column structure and all text content unchanged. Reduce card height, make content fit tightly with the bottom label right after content.

Approach: make cards height auto-ish? But slide is fixed 1080 height. Better approach: use flex column with the card heights reduced to e.g. 320px, and position cards at top:474px. Or convert cards to inline-flex auto height with justify-content between removed.

Simplest: change .card to height:340px, padding reduced, card-body flex:1 removed -> so foot sits right after body. Actually with card-body flex:1 removed, foot will follow content naturally, but card has fixed height so foot would be right after content, leaving whitespace at bottom of card. Better: make card height auto (no fixed height) and use display:flex column; then footer rule stays at 960. Cards at top 474, content height ~ let's compute.

Let me estimate content heights: padding top 40, card-top ~48 (num 40px), card-body margin-top 34 + content. For c1: key 40px font, line-height1.5 → 60px, one line? "连接参数与多工况响应的联合分析" at 40px = 16 chars × ~40px = 640px width > 470px available → wraps to 2 lines = 120px. Then sub-line 22px margin + 18px font line-height 1.7 = 30.6 × maybe 2 lines = 61. So body ≈ 34+120+22+61 = 237. plus top 40 + card-top 48 = 325, plus card-foot margin 18 + padding 14 + text 13*? ~ 18+1+14+16=49 → total ≈ 374.

Hmm, c1 is the tallest. Others shorter. To balance visual weight, I could let all cards have same height (auto) — but flex items in absolute positioning won't equalize. Alternative: set explicit height for each card? The instruction says "降低卡片高度使三栏高度与正文量匹配" — lower card height so the three columns' heights match their content volume, i.e., each card height fits its content, eliminating whitespace. So auto height per card is exactly right.

So: .card { height:auto; display:flex; flex-direction:column; } .card-body { flex:none; margin-top:26px } .card-foot { margin-top:22px; ... }

But then the three cards will have different heights — "使三栏视觉重量均衡" (balance visual weight). Hmm, different heights but no whitespace. Maybe give each card a min-height and let content define. Actually with auto heights, c1 ~374, c2 shorter, c3 shorter. Bottom edges uneven — that could look unbalanced. Perhaps better: keep equal heights but reduce to the max needed (~380), and put footer label right after content (flex:1 removed) so no gap inside. Equal heights ~ 390px, footer at ~ 474+390 = 864, bottom rule at 960. That leaves ~96px gap to bottom rule — acceptable, less than before (before card ended at 902).

Hmm but then c2 and c3 have whitespace at their bottoms because equal height with less content. Instruction: "将底部标签上移紧贴正文，消除下半部大面积留白" — move footer labels up close to the body text. That implies cards where body has flex:1 pushing footer to bottom now the footer sits right after text. If heights equal, then shorter cards would have empty space below the footer... that is weird too but the footer would be right under text, and card bottom would extend below. Hmm.

Better design: auto-height cards with content-driven heights, but visually balanced by placing them on a common baseline area? Different heights is fine — many editorial layouts do that. But "视觉重量均衡" — balanced visual weight.

Alternative approach: make cards auto-height but add a bottom accent / the foot rule stays. To balance weight, I could reduce the content size of c1 slightly (key font from 40 to 34) so heights closer.

Let me just do: cards auto height, c1 key font 34px so it fits 2 lines within 470px? At 34px, 16 chars ≈ 544 > 470 → 2 lines. Hmm still 2 lines. If reduce to 30px: 16×30=480 ≈ 470 → borderline. Keep 2 lines but smaller.

Compute heights with auto:
- Common: padding 36 top, card-top (num 36px line 1) ≈ 40.
- body margin-top 26.
- c1: key 34px lh 1.5 = 51 ×2 = 102; sub-line margin 20 + 17px×1.7=29 ×1 line (text "拟议创新点即在于上述两个方面的联合分析。" 19 chars at 17px = 323 < 470 → 1 line) = 49. body = 26+102+49 = 177.
- foot: margin-top 20 + border-top + padding-top 12 + 14px text ~17 = 50.
- total c1 ≈ 36+40+177+50+36(bottom padding) = 339.

- c2: strong 26px lh1.6=41.6 (1 line? "定位为拟议方向" 7 chars×26=182 fits) = 42; mini-rule margin 24+1+24=49; note 22px lh1.75 = 38.5 × "不表述为已证实的技术领先或确定性能提升。" 20 chars × 22 = 440 < 470 → 1 line? Available width = 552-2*40 = 472. 440 fits barely → 1 line = 39. body = 26+42+49+39 = 156. total ≈ 36+40+156+50+36 = 318.

- c3: note 22px: "创新性结论需在试验完成后检验。" 15 chars ×22 = 330 → 1 line = 39; marker margin-top 26 + padding 7*2 + 14px text ~17 → 26+14+17=57. body = 26+39+57=122. total ≈ 36+40+122+50+36 = 284.

Heights 339, 318, 284 — reasonably close. Uneven bottoms though. Could align by setting them all to a fixed height of 340 with footers right after content — then c3's card bottom would have 56px gap after footer. Hmm.

Maybe better: keep equal heights but reduce to 340 (from 428), and align footers to bottom? No — instruction says move footers up to hug the text.

Compromise: fixed height 344 for all three cards (uniform bottom edge = balanced visual weight), footer labels positioned right after content (not pushed to bottom). Some whitespace remains at bottom of c2/c3 cards, but much less than before, and bottoms align. Hmm, but instruction explicitly says "将底部标签上移紧贴正文，消除下半部大面积留白".

I think auto height with different bottoms is riskier for "视觉重量均衡"? Actually the ask: "降低卡片高度使三栏高度与正文量匹配" — lower card heights so the columns' heights match content volume. This literally means per-card height matches its content. So auto height. And "三栏视觉重量均衡" means no column is dominated by whitespace.

I'll go with auto heights + footer hugging content. To reduce unevenness, I can add a small accent element or just accept. Alternatively, align cards to a common top and add a thin baseline tick under each card bottom? Hmm, could add a subtle vertical accent line at the bottom of each card extending to a common line — too fancy.

Another option: make cards auto height and then place a shared horizontal "ground line" at, say, y=880 that all three cards sit above with a small tick connector — visually balances tops/middles. That adds non-factual decoration, which is fine.

Hmm, but keep it simple and clean. I'll do: cards auto height, top:474px, and a subtle baseline rule at y=860 connecting? Actually the foot-rule at 960 exists.

Let me instead position cards with align items and let their tops vary? No — keep tops aligned.

Decision: auto-height cards, footer label immediately after content with a border-top rule. To balance, add a small colored block per card at the bottom? Simpler: keep it.

Actually, another balance idea: give each card a min-height so they're close: min-height 330? c3 = 284 → grows to 330 with footer hugging text and 46px empty at bottom. Meh.

I'll just use auto heights. Also I should nudge card top position: previously 474. With shorter cards, maybe center block vertically between 474 and 960? Content region: head-rule at 372, lead 396-~440. Cards top 474 is fine; below cards region 474-960 total 486 while cards ~340 → leftover 146 at bottom before foot rule. Could move cards down a bit to top:500 for better balance. 474+340=814, gap to 960 = 146. If top=520, bottom=860, gap 100 — better balance. Lead ends around y = 396 + 2 lines×35.7 ≈ 468. So cards at 500 or 510 OK.

Let me set cards top: 508px. Then bottoms ≈ 847, 826, 792. Gap to foot-rule 960: 113. Reasonable.

Hmm, maybe also widen the vertical gap by adding a subtle "ground" line at 880? Not necessary. Let's keep clean.

Actually to make the three columns look balanced despite different heights, I could give each card bottom a small numbered baseline tick spanning card width — like a bottom edge accent of 4px colored. Card has :before top accent; add :after bottom accent 2px. That gives a firm bottom edge for each, feeling intentional. But different heights still.

Alternatively use align-items to stretch? Position cards as flex siblings in a container with align-items:stretch — then equal heights automatically equal to tallest (339). Then footers hug text with flex:none... whitespace appears at bottom of shorter cards but bottoms aligned. Hmm. That's arguably most balanced visually. But instruction wants reduced whitespace.

I'll go with auto heights + bottom hairline accent. Good enough.

Wait — a potential issue: the marker in c3 "待试验完成后检验" plus note.

Let's also adjust .card padding to 36px 38px 32px.

Font sizes: keep all text content, can adjust sizes slightly for density (allowed: "只调整密度" - only adjust density). I'll keep most sizes, maybe reduce key from 40→36, strong 26→25, note 22→21. Keep legibility.

Actually careful: reducing font sizes is adjusting density, allowed. But let's keep them fairly large for a 1920 canvas.

Heights recompute:
c1: padding-top 34 + card-top(num 40 lh1 → 40; tag aligned) 40 + body(24 + key 36*1.45=52.2 ×2 lines=104 + sub 18+29=47) = 175 + foot(22+1+12+17=52) + padding-bottom 30 = 331.
c2: 34+40+ (24+25*1.6=40 +20+1+20=41 + 21*1.7=36) = 24+40+41+36=141 +52 +30 = 297.
c3: 34+40+(24+36+22+14+17=113)+52+30 = 269.

Bottoms: 508+331=839, 805, 777. Differences up to 62px. Hmm, c3 noticeably shorter.

Could reduce c1 height by keeping key on... it's fine. Maybe make c3 marker add more? No, can't add content.

Maybe equalize with min-height on each: give c2 min-height 300, c3 min-height 300? with foot hugging text, whitespace 30px at bottom. Eh.

Alternatively vertically center each card's content? Cards top-aligned is standard.

Accept. Actually I could adjust tops so bottoms align? No, tops should align.

Alternative: use a flex row container with align-items:flex-start and each card auto height — same as absolute. Fine.

Let me maybe add a faint vertical "column spine" behind each card extending down to a common baseline (e.g., to y=860) so the three columns visually terminate together. Actually simpler: below the cards, add nothing; the foot-rule at 960 closes it.

Hmm, to reduce perceived imbalance, maybe place cards so their bottoms are near a common area and add small index numbers under each card at a common baseline y=880? That's the "COLUMN" markers — decorative, no facts. That would tie the row together: three small ticks + the label. But the card-foot labels already serve that function inside cards.

I'll add a subtle common baseline: a thin horizontal line at y=872 from x=96 to x=1824 with low opacity? Cards bottom at 839/805/777 — the line at 872 sits below all, forming a ground line. Then each card connects? Without connectors, it's just a line. Could add short vertical ticks from card bottom to the line — that would look like dimension lines and unify. Nice touch: for each card, a 1px vertical line from card bottom down to y=872 at the left edge (x=96, 684, 1272). Hmm, but the differing lengths reveal imbalance. Actually it makes it look intentional/technical.

Might be over-engineering. Simpler: put a small "ground rule" at 872 spanning the three card widths with tick marks. Let me skip and just ensure foot rule at 960.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider: maybe keep uniform card heights (all 340, tops at 508 → bottom 848) with footers hugging text. Then all three bottoms align → clean grid; some cards have trailing whitespace of ~50-70px inside card bottom. The original problem was 428 height with footer pushed to bottom (large gap between text and footer + gap below). With 340 and footers hugging, the gap is only below the footer, small.

Comparing: uniform 340 with aligned bottoms looks better typographically. But instruction "降低卡片高度使三栏高度与正文量匹配" — match content volume. With uniform 340, c1 is exactly full (331≈340), c2 has 43px slack, c3 has 71px slack. That's still "reduced whitespace". And "三栏视觉重量均衡" — aligned bottoms help.

I think a hybrid is best: auto heights (no fixed) so content drives, giving natural minimal whitespace. Reviewers of the instruction would check: card height reduced ✓, footer labels moved up hugging text ✓, no large whitespace at bottom ✓. Uneven bottoms is a minor aesthetic risk but the instruction explicitly frames height per content volume.

Hmm, "使三栏视觉重量均衡" — balanced visual weight across three columns. With auto heights, columns have different masses but no dead space; roughly balanced already since heights within 60px.

I'll go with auto height. And I'll reduce card top to 500 and add the foot rule unchanged at 960. Also maybe move the lead/cards spacing: card top 500 fine (lead ends ~468).

Wait, lead is width 1180 at top 396, font 21 line-height 1.7 = 35.7; text: "本页陈述拟议创新点、其表述边界与检验条件；以下内容为拟议方向，非已完成的实验结论。" ~42 chars × 21 = 882 < 1180 → 1 line, ends at ~432. So cards could start higher, e.g., 470. Then bottoms 801/775/739 → gap to 960 rule = 159/185/221. Worse. So keeping cards lower (500-520) is better for filling vertical space.

Let's set card top: 516px. Bottoms: 847/813/785. Gap to foot rule: 113/147/175. Hmm.

Alternatively increase content sizes a bit. Keep as planned; maybe enlarge key font back toward 38 for c1 weight.

Let me also consider making cards a bit wider? No, three columns fixed.

I'll finalize. Also add to cards: a bottom hairline accent for grounding.

Let me write final HTML with only CSS density changes (structure/text unchanged).

Also adjust .card-foot letter-spacing etc. Keep same labels.
